title: intermittent-shadow-peeker-session-coherent-replayable-rollback
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: We need a lightweight, low-cost way to surface intermittently occurring regressions (tail quality and tail latency) that are missed by steady shadow mirroring and typical canaries. This PR implements an "intermittent shadow peeker" mode plus session-coherent cutover semantics and a deterministic rollback/replay path for reproducible remediation.

Summary of changes: introduces an intermittent sampling controller (configurable cadence and burst window) that temporarily mirrors a small fraction of traffic to candidate variants with tightened telemetry (percentile stratification, session-level correlation) and preserves session affinity and KV-cache continuity during cutover phases. Adds an input-snapshotting facility that records deterministic request vectors and minimal state needed to replay sessions on a reference infra for rollback validation. Exposes rollout policies to the orchestration layer so automated rollback can invoke replay checks before finalizing a revert.

Key user-visible behavior:
- "peeker" sampling windows: short-lived high-fidelity shadow bursts (default 30s every 15min) that increase sensitivity to transient regressions without continuous cost.
- Session-coherent cutover: when promoting a variant from peeker/canary to live, the controller migrates session affinity and checkpoints KV-cache keys referenced during peeker windows to avoid cold-cache regressions.
- Replayable rollback: on a rollback trigger, the system can perform deterministic replay of recorded sessions against the to-be-restored variant and produce a traceable diff artifact (response deltas, latency histogram deltas, token-level divergence).

Design notes: The intermittent peeker leverages our existing router token to divert a configurable traffic shard and attaches a short-lived mirror session tag. Peeker telemetry enriches spans with sample-tier labels and computes 50/90/95/99 tail deltas. The rollback replay engine is deliberately minimal — it captures request inputs, model version, K/V dependencies (keys touched), and sequence seeds to allow deterministic re-execution on the same model binary. This avoids shipping full recordings of payloads beyond what is necessary for verification (privacy conscious config).

Compatibility and safety: Default config is opt-in per-route. Peeker windows are rate-limited and subject to existing tenant quotas. Replay recordings are encrypted at rest and access-controlled by RBAC. No change to default routing semantics for routes that do not opt into peeker.

Testing: added unit tests for sampling controller, end-to-end integ test that simulates a tail-latency spike during peeker bursts, and a replay smoke test that validates deterministic replays on toy models. Also ran canary on infra (dedicated test cluster) for 48 hours.

Checklist:
- [x] Implementation of intermittent peeker controller and policy bindings
- [x] Session-coherent cutover logic and KV checkpointing
- [x] Deterministic replay capture format and minimal replay engine
- [x] Unit/integration tests and basic canary run
- [x] Docs (console toggle + rollout recipe)

Notes for reviewers: focus on safety boundaries (quota enforcement, privacy knobs), replay determinism guarantees, and any implications for autoscaling during burst windows. Related: ENG-3142 describes evaluation criteria; SUP-7812 was filed after a customer incident where transient tail regressions escaped detection.

review_comments: Diego Alvarez: overall this looks good; two questions: how do we guarantee no extra cost leak to shared routing components? can we add telemetry for peeker admission failures?
Maya Chen: reply: peeker admission is enforced at router edge and we've added admission counters and a peeker_admit_failure metric (see mirroring_tags.go); added test to assert quota enforcement.
Priya Nair: please ensure replay captures are privacy-filtered and include a retention TTL default. Also would like a knob to disable storing K/V snapshots at customer request.
Maya Chen: reply: added privacy filter hook and retention TTL config (default 7d). K/V snapshotting can be disabled per-tenant via rollout policy (see session_checkpoint.go).
Liam O'Connor: minor: prefer 'burst_window' naming consistency (we had 'burstWindow' in some places). Also can we add a quick chart to the console docs showing expected cost vs sensitivity?
Maya Chen: reply: normalized naming to 'burst_window' across controller and console, and added a cost/sensitivity chart to docs.
merge_details: Merged via squash by Diego Alvarez on 2026-02-03. Commit message: intermittent peeker: session coherent cutover + replayable rollback (ENG-3142)
release_notes: Adds an opt-in 'intermittent shadow peeker' sampling mode that surfaces transient regressions with low continuous cost, session-coherent cutover to avoid cold-cache regressions during promotions, and a minimal deterministic replay path for reproducible rollback verification. Opt-in per-route; privacy and quota controls included.
notes_for_ops: Monitor metrics: peeker.admit_count, peeker.admit_failures, peeker.tail_delta_p95/p99, replay.verification_pass_rate. Default cost exposure is low but watch burst_window concurrently with autoscaler settings. If replay runs fail due to non-determinism, buffer and alert to oncall for manual review.
testing_summary: Unit coverage added for controller and replay capture; integration test simulates transient latency/payload shifts and validates detection during peeker bursts; canary run on dedicated test infra for 48h confirmed no regressions in default traffic paths.
backport_recommendation: backport to release/2026-01 only if customers opt into peeker in production; otherwise ship in next minor. Backport should include quota enforcement patch (0a9d3c4).
